title: I'm building a tool that turns game devlogs into videos, so I can focus on making games
author: Sudden_Network621
selftext:
I love building games. What I don't love is everything that comes after: making social media content, editing videos, writing posts, writing devlogs and constantly trying to get people interested in what I'm building.

So I started building **Devstory** for myself.

The idea is pretty simple. A little desktop companion called Nim observes your development process and automatically collects progress logs, screenshots, artwork, gameplay clips and turn them into a devlog. 

But the main goal isn't just writing devlogs.

**I want Devstory to turn those logs into engaging short documentary videos about the actual development journey.**

Not generic AI-generated promotional videos. Real stories about what you're building, what went wrong, what changed, and how your game evolved.

Ideally, you just develop your game and come back to find potential stories ready to turn into videos.

I'm also working on a website where developers can optionally publish their devlogs and showcase games that are still in development. Hopefully, that gives people another way to discover interesting indie projects.

It's still an early prototype, and the automated video pipeline isn't finished yet. I made this trailer to show where I want to take it.

**I'm curious about two things:**

1. Do you struggle with promoting your games as much as I do?
2. Would you actually use something that turns your development progress into ready-to-post videos?

I'm building this because I genuinely want to spend more time making games and less time marketing them. Curious whether other indie devs feel the same.

replies.author: fremdspielen
replies.body:
I think it could meet the devlog category, but not the others. A few thoughts because I find the idea intriguing, and I have the same "i want to keep building" conflict of interest.

Trailer/doku/series (whatever series is) production requirements IMO do not fit the "keeps me building" as you'd still (have to, should) spend days to weeks on these. Trailer needs high quality content, your tool could help capture some of that but you'd still have to review a lot of it and still create custom takes and refine it a lot to meet the 30-60s window and an intense arch, plus you'd want snappy cuts and all those fancy effects.

Doku requires additional content on top, ie references to other games, tools, builders, websites, etc. plus all the narration - a documentary end-to-end does not write itself, not even with AI. AI will give you terrible scripts without excellent prompting and a lot of material to feed it with. Best use: have it structurally sort the talking points (a few words per talking point) so the documentary catches interest, keeps the interest, and has an outcome viewers crave for. Then query it for insights on every talking point. Just to get the documentary story arch for a 10-15 minute video is likely a day's work.

Devlogs are fine having a one-shot feel though, so I'd focus on that specifically because it also best fits your requirements, the others would be distractions in building the tool and dilute the experience.

I'd hope for a configurable, system-wide hotkey to take screenshots and capture video - ideally with an event you can capture in-editor (any application) so you can start for instance the Unity Recorder with a given preset because you do not want to have to deal with things like: what window / part of the screen to capture at what quality using which codec.

Taking automatic screenshots is a bit problematic because of the sheer amount, and many shots not showing something meaningful ie you answering to my post on Reddit. ;)  
Unless it's manual and then you'd forget taking shots, or the shots are rather selective ie a lot of art progress but nothing about the new features.

Screenshots would also require minimal cropping tools, assuming the shot is a fullscreen desktop grab which would capture the Windows taskbar too. I have a 32:9 monitor, none of my applications run maximized, that's another reason.

Again, I think this has merit but I'd start it small and laser focused because there's a lot of gotchas that can cause issues and scope creep.

replies.author: Sudden_Network621
replies.body:
I actually agree with you on that. I don’t want more generic AI written LinkedIn posts either.

The whole reason I’m building this is because I enjoy following the actual development journey, including the struggles, failed attempts, weird decisions and little breakthroughs.

The idea is to capture what really happened while developing, preserve the original artwork and gameplay, and use that to create short documentary style videos. Not invent some inspirational founder story or turn everything into an ad.

And if nothing interesting happened that day, there’s no reason to force a post. That’s also why I’m testing this publicly. I want to find out whether AI can genuinely help tell those stories without making everything feel artificial.
